messages:
Camila Torres: FYI I dropped a first-pass PRD for the "Insights: storage, retention & export" initiative — link in doc. Core asks: per-route retention tiers, one-click export to object stores, migration UI, and console visibility for query costs. Can folks review ACs + edge cases by EOD Fri?

Michael Chen: Quick clarification — do customers expect retention scoped to a route (user feature) or to a model variant? Asking because API shape differs.

Anya Patel: UX opinion: route-level is the mental model customers use. I'll prototype a route settings panel showing "effective retention" and a shrink warning.

Derek Liu: Infra note: per-route retention -> metadata explosion. Proposed approach: group routes into retention buckets (hot/standard/cold) and store per-route override metadata only when non-default. Backfill cost estimate for 90->365 for a typical mid market org ~= 2.5k GPU-hours; will validate.

Sophie Nguyen: Also: queries that cross hot/cold will show higher p99. Recommend adding a console signal ("estimated query cost + expected latency") and an opt-in async historical query path for exports.

Camila Torres: Draft acceptance criteria I'm adding now: 1) Console: per-route retention selector with presets [30, 90, 365] and custom up to 1095. 2) Export: `POST /routes/:id/exports` -> resumable job with checksum manifest. 3) Migration: cancelable backfill jobs with progress UI. 4) Observability: per-route token/storage estimate + latency histogram. 5) Rollout plan: staged canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic 30d fallback on failures.

Michael Chen: API sketches I'll add: `PATCH /routes/:id` payload `{ "retention_days": 90, "count_based_retention": false }`. For exports, manifest fields: `route_id`, `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `object_path`, `sha256_digest`, `record_count`. Also RBAC checks — only admins or route owners can reduce retention.

Anya Patel: Design notes: shrink retention modal must show estimated migration cost and a clear "undo" window. Goal: change retention in <= 2 clicks. I have 3 mock variants; uploading to the doc now.

Derek Liu: Edge cases to capture in PRD: 1) pinned KV entries or long-lived cache references — token-count vs timestamp retention mismatch. Propose `count_based_retention` toggle per-route. 2) Partial export resume semantics for interrupted jobs. 3) Enforced deletion window: enforcement runs hourly; callers should not rely on immediate purge.

Sophie Nguyen: SLOs and alerts: backfill must not spike error rate > 0.1%. Online query p99 must not worsen >20% vs baseline during backfills. Add alerts for export failures >3 retries and migration jobs stuck >24h.

Camila Torres: Legal/customer request: e-discovery export format. Michael/Derek, please add required fields and sample manifest. Should include hashes and a human-readable index.

Michael Chen: I added a YAML example in the doc and sample API contract. Example manifest: ```{ "route_id": "r_abc123", "start_ts": 1672531200, "end_ts": 1675133200, "objects": [ { "path": "s3://company-exports/r_abc123/part-0001.ndjson.gz", "sha256": "...", "count": 12000 } ], "generated_by": "redwood-exporter-v1", "generated_at": 1823456900 }```

Derek Liu: Will implement export resumability via job checkpoints and object-level checksums. Also noting retention enforcement: deletion sweeper runs hourly; for immediate legal holds we need a `hold` flag that prevents deletion. Add to PRD.

ops-bot: Doc updated: https://docs.internal/redwood/insights-storage-prd (edited by Camila Torres) :white_check_mark:

Anya Patel: Designs posted. I added the modal copy and the inline cost estimate widget.

Camila Torres: Thanks — I'll fold these into the PRD and ping again once infra numbers are finalized. If anyone can't meet EOD Fri for comments please flag here now.
